newsitem.title: USA: Stocks bow to more profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Stocks bow to more profit-taking.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell Thursday as the market was rattled by a second straight day of selling pressure after the recent rise to record highs.
The Dow Jones industrial average dropped 27.05 points to 7,330.18 after falling 26 points on Wednesday.
But in the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,435 to 1,043 on moderate volume 460.5 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index lost 7.14 points to 1,403.04.
Investors turned up the pressure on technology stocks, which had provided much of the market's recent strength.
International Business Machines Corp. tumbled 2-1/4 to 87-7/8 and the shares of computer network companies also got clobbered after big recent gains.

"A lot of these tech stocks had made ferocious runs in a very volatile market," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "Wall Street always tends to go to extremes and there's always a snapback afterwards."
Among networking stocks, 3Com Corp. fell 3-5/16 to 47-3/16 after rising nearly 10 points in the last week. Ascend Communications lost 2-3/4 to 56-5/8 after a similar run.
With many major indexes near record highs, analysts said they detected a cautious mood among investors.
Several key economic reports are due over the next week, they noted, which also prodded investors to lock in profits from the market's six-week surge.
"We have a couple of pieces of data coming up that are going to be very important," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
Next week the government will issue the May jobs report and the nation's purchasing managers' will report on industrial activity in June.

On Friday the government will revise its initial reading of the economy's first-quarter performance, a report likely to draw attention because of the strong growth already recorded. Economists forecast a revision to a 6.0 percent annual growth rate for the quarter from the initial 5.6 percent rate.
Some analysts wondered if even those forecasts, which are more than double the growth rate the Federal Reserve is believed to target, are high enough.

"We think the potential exists for a positive surprise there and that second quarter GDP could also come in above current expectations," Orlando said. "All that suggests the Fed erred by not tightening" at its last interest rate policy meeting earlier this month.
The Fed decided on May 20 to leave interest rates unchanged after raising short-term rates a quarter point in March in a bid to slow the economy and ward off inflation.

Worries about higher rates failed to shake bond traders, as the market turned in a solid performance. The benchmark 30-year Treasury rose 20/32, or $6.25 on a $1,000 bond, cutting its yield to 6.98 percent from 7.03 percent on Wednesday. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Personal computer makers posted steep losses, hit by negative comments from several analysts.
Salomon Brothers lowered its rating on IBM, helping spur the broad decline in the group. Gateway 2000 Inc. lost 5-7/8 to 68-1/2 and Compaq Computer Corp. fell five to 101-3/4.

Nike Inc. skidded 8-5/8 to 55-3/8. The athletic footwear maker warned that its fourth quarter earnings would be lower than Wall Street estimates, a development that wiped out a two-day, largely rumour-driven, rally in the shares.
Gucci Group NV fell 5-7/8 to 68-1/2. The luxury goods maker told analysts April sales were hurt by the weak Japanese yen.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 3.13 points to 844.08. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.33 to 603.12.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.80 to 438.86. The average share was down 7 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,900.970 down 12.078 or 0.15 percent.
